open_points.subject: trial execution input materialization
open_points.text: “Each case, in corpus order, is one call of capability:sandbox.execute_function with the implementation's code, the case's inputs and the contract's bounds”
open_points.question: Who reads the StoredValue and file-fixture bytes for a trial case, decodes them, and supplies the concrete Python inputs to the sandbox?
options: module:functions reads them through capability:store.read_value_bytes and passes concrete inputs
module:sandbox receives references and reads their bytes
module:store prepares the complete sandbox input
open_points.default_guess: module:functions reads the bytes through capability:store.read_value_bytes, decodes value carriage, and passes concrete values and file bytes to module:sandbox

open_points.subject: flow constant persistence
open_points.text: “A new version is written with its constants, each with the class the agent declared”
open_points.question: Which step publishes each constant's bytes in the content-addressed area before its StoredValue and FlowVersion references are written?
options: module:flows calls capability:store.put_value_bytes before record_change
record_change also accepts and publishes value bytes
constants are stored inline in the FlowVersion
open_points.default_guess: module:flows calls capability:store.put_value_bytes, then writes the StoredValue references and FlowVersion

open_points.subject: run input persistence
open_points.text: “writes the Run running with its pins, starter and start time … and the input values with their identities”
open_points.question: Which capability publishes the run input bytes required by their StoredValue records?
options: module:runs calls capability:store.put_value_bytes before writing the run records
the run record_change publishes both bytes and records
the request body remains the byte source for the life of the run
open_points.default_guess: module:runs calls capability:store.put_value_bytes and then writes the StoredValues and Run

open_points.subject: function output persistence during a run
open_points.text: “module:runs writes the element's NodeExecution and the outputs”
open_points.question: Who publishes successful value-output bytes before the NodeExecution and downstream records refer to their StoredValues?
options: module:runs calls capability:store.put_value_bytes
module:sandbox publishes the bytes
record_change accepts payload bytes as part of the trace write
open_points.default_guess: module:runs calls capability:store.put_value_bytes before its record_change

open_points.subject: service output persistence
open_points.text: “module:effects writes the concluding NodeExecution and the output values”
open_points.question: Who publishes value-output bytes returned by a service in both read and effectful runs before records refer to their StoredValues?
options: module:effects calls capability:store.put_value_bytes
module:service_invoker publishes the values
the effects outcome record_change also publishes payload bytes
open_points.default_guess: module:effects calls capability:store.put_value_bytes before writing the outcome records

open_points.subject: operation request value materialization
open_points.text: “JSON values are placed as capability:canonical_values.canonical_bytes, and file inputs are read through capability:store.read_value_bytes”
open_points.question: Who reads and decodes value-carriage StoredValues before service_invoker can canonicalize them into path, query, JSON, or multipart fields?
options: module:effects reads them through capability:store.read_value_bytes
module:runs passes concrete values rather than record references
module:service_invoker reads StoredValues itself
open_points.default_guess: module:effects reads and decodes value-carriage inputs through capability:store.read_value_bytes before calling service_invoker

open_points.subject: guard evaluation and edge delivery
open_points.text: “module:runs writes the skips and upstream failures that became determined”
open_points.question: Which capability supplies the actual stored value needed to compare a guard after restart or when the producing value is no longer in memory?
options: module:runs reads it through capability:store.read_value_bytes
guard values are copied into NodeExecution records
module:flows evaluates guards from stored records
open_points.default_guess: module:runs reads and decodes the guarded StoredValue through capability:store.read_value_bytes

open_points.subject: captured value inputs
open_points.text: “writes the file-carriage StoredValues, each with the class its contract input port declares … and the TrialCase”
open_points.question: For captured value-carriage inputs whose existing StoredValue has a lower runtime class than the contract input port's declared class, who creates the required trial-case StoredValue with the contract-port class?
options: module:functions reads the existing bytes and writes a new StoredValue identity with the contract-port class
the captured TrialCase reuses the existing StoredValue despite its different class
capture changes the class on the existing StoredValue
open_points.default_guess: module:functions reuses the content bytes but writes or resolves a StoredValue identity carrying the contract input port's class

open_points.subject: recovery after an unknown attempt was resolved not_applied
open_points.text: “an attempt the owner resolved concludes from its records and is not reached again”
open_points.question: If the process stopped after recording resolution not_applied but before requesting the mandatory fresh approval, must recovery reach the element to create that approval, or must it leave the element unreached?
options: Reach the element again only to perform pre-send checks and request the fresh approval for the next attempt
Never reach an element whose prior attempt has any owner resolution
Derive an owner_approval wait without creating an EffectApproval
open_points.default_guess: Reach the element again to request the fresh approval; do not resend or recreate the resolved attempt

open_points.subject: failure to remove a run spool
open_points.text: “a store call that fails changes no record … and the request is answered as an internal error” versus “a removal that fails or is interrupted fails nothing”
open_points.question: When capability:store.remove_run_spool fails during normal run completion, cancellation, refusal, or release, does the request fail with internal_error and stop the kernel, or does the run action succeed with cleanup deferred to startup?
options: The run action succeeds and cleanup is retried at startup
The committed run action stands, but the response is internal_error and the kernel stops
The run action and its record are rolled back
open_points.default_guess: The committed run action succeeds; leftover spool files are never served and cleanup is retried at startup
